text:
Macklin Celebrini has 18 points in nine career games against Minnesota, per Sharks Hockey Digest's Max Miller, and the Wild still won 5-2 in San Jose on Monday. That's the Sharks right now: a star and a rookie class worth the ticket, and a team that gives up too much.

The good part is easy to see. Celebrini and Will Smith have taken 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with either Igor Chernyshov or Ivar Stenberg on the other wing, in samples of about an hour each. NHL.com's Rookie Watch has Stenberg trending up, and Michael Misa has a four-game point streak. Dmitry Orlov has 11 points in his last 10 games on 5.0 expected, which will cool.

The rest is a rebuild's numbers. San Jose is 11-13-2 with 44% of the expected goals, it allows 3.77 expected goals per 60, and the penalty kill gives up 0.97 expected goals a game. The Darnell Nurse and Michael Kesselring pair has been on for 6 goals for and 15 against at 5-on-5, and Stenberg's line with Kiefer Sherwood and Misa gets only 34% of the chances. The Sharks have scored about nine fewer goals than their chances predict and allowed about eight fewer, so the luck roughly cancels.

Our playoff odds are 7%. What we'd watch: how Ryan Warsofsky balances minutes for the kids against a defence that needs help.
headline: Celebrini's Sharks: a real top line, a leaky team
